isolation.reason: Statutory vocabulary overlaps the generic high-frequency tokens that carry routing in haven_purpose_knowledge_base_index_v0.json. Eight candidate nodes previously moved evaluate_purpose_cases.mjs from 56/56 to 53/56. This overlay is kept in a separate artifact with a separate index and is reachable only by explicit ref lookup or by classification of a declared purpose, never by free-text prompt routing.

legalSource.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
legalSource.consolidationNote: Dates below reflect the Digital Omnibus amendments as reported by secondary sources on 2026-08-18. Article text has NOT been read from EUR-Lex article-by-article for this research run. Every node carries textSourceStatus to make that explicit.

vocabularyNote: triggerTokens are drawn from statutory wording only. HAVEN vocabulary was deliberately not consulted when authoring them, so that run A measures a genuine vocabulary gap rather than a rigged match.

facetAxes.note: These are the five declared facets a HAVEN purpose node would need for rule-based derivation (run B). They are the proposed schema addition.

nodes.title: Subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques
nodes.statutoryCore: Placing on the market, putting into service or use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting behaviour by appreciably impairing the ability to make an informed decision, causing significant harm.
nodes.derivationRule: aiInvolvement != none AND decisionEffect in [influences-human-decision, automated-decision-with-legal-or-similar-effect] AND intentToInfluence == true

nodes.title: Exploiting vulnerabilities of age, disability or socio-economic situation
nodes.statutoryCore: Exploiting any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or effect of materially distorting behaviour in a manner that causes significant harm.
nodes.derivationRule: dataSubjects == vulnerable-groups AND decisionEffect != none AND aiInvolvement != none

nodes.title: Social scoring
nodes.statutoryCore: Evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups over a period of time based on social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics, leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment in unrelated social contexts or that is unjustified or disproportionate.
nodes.derivationRule: dataSubjects in [named-third-parties, public] AND producesPersonScore == true AND decisionEffect != none
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: HAVEN's stated design position is the negation of this practice. The interesting test is whether the negation is machine-checkable, not whether the practice is present.

nodes.title: Predicting criminal offence risk based solely on profiling or personality traits
nodes.statutoryCore: Risk assessments of natural persons to assess or predict the risk of committing a criminal offence, based solely on profiling or on assessing personality traits and characteristics.

nodes.title: Untargeted scraping of facial images
nodes.statutoryCore: Creating or expanding facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage.

nodes.title: Emotion inference in the workplace and in education institutions
nodes.statutoryCore: Inferring emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where intended for medical or safety reasons.
nodes.derivationRule: domain in [employment, education] AND infersEmotion == true
nodes.havenTestForm: negative test against the capability registry: no registered Cell exposes an emotion or sentiment inference capability in an employment or education scaffold.

nodes.title: Biometric categorisation deducing sensitive attributes
nodes.statutoryCore: Biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation.
nodes.havenTestForm: negative test against the capability registry.

nodes.title: Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement
nodes.statutoryCore: Use of real-time remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement, subject to narrow enumerated exceptions and prior authorisation.
nodes.derivationRule: domain == biometrics AND realTimeRemote == true AND domainSecondary == law-enforcement

nodes.title: Generation of non-consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material
nodes.statutoryCore: Prohibition added by the Digital Omnibus, extending beyond systems intentionally designed for the purpose to systems where such generation is a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification, absent adequate safeguards.
nodes.derivationRule: outputModality == synthetic-media AND aiInvolvement == model-generated AND safeguardEvidence == absent
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: Relevant to HAVEN as a routing layer to third-party image/multimodal models, not as an image generator itself. The duty attaches to the safeguard evidence, not to the intent.

nodes.title: Biometrics
nodes.statutoryCore: Remote biometric identification systems; biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes; emotion recognition systems.

nodes.title: Critical infrastructure
nodes.statutoryCore: Safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.

nodes.title: Education and vocational training
nodes.statutoryCore: Determining access or admission; evaluating learning outcomes; assessing the appropriate level of education a person will receive; monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour during tests.

nodes.title: Employment, workers management and access to self-employment
nodes.statutoryCore: Recruitment or selection, in particular targeted job advertisements, analysing and filtering applications and evaluating candidates; and decisions affecting terms of work-related relationships, promotion or termination, allocation of tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, and monitoring and evaluating performance and behaviour of persons in such relationships.
nodes.derivationRule: domain == employment AND (allocatesTasksToPersons == true OR evaluatesPersonPerformance == true)
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: The one Annex III area with a plausible, non-hypothetical path into current HAVEN functionality, via project and work-item tracking.

nodes.title: Access to essential private and public services
nodes.statutoryCore: Eligibility for public assistance benefits and services; creditworthiness evaluation and credit scoring; risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance; classification of emergency calls and dispatch of emergency services.
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: Worth checking against DiMy value-return and entitlement mechanics rather than against CellProtocol.

nodes.title: Law enforcement
nodes.statutoryCore: Victim risk assessment; polygraphs; evaluating reliability of evidence; assessing risk of offending or re-offending; profiling in the course of detection, investigation or prosecution.

nodes.title: Migration, asylum and border control management
nodes.statutoryCore: Polygraphs; assessing security, health or irregular migration risk; examining applications for asylum, visa or residence permits; detecting, recognising or identifying persons, excluding verification of travel documents.

nodes.title: Administration of justice and democratic processes
nodes.statutoryCore: Assisting a judicial authority in researching and interpreting facts and the law and in applying the law to a concrete set of facts; and influencing the outcome of an election or referendum or the voting behaviour of natural persons.
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: Note the second limb. A system that influences voting behaviour is high-risk regardless of who operates it. Relevant to any future HAVEN deliberation or civic-participation surface.

nodes.title: Disclose that the person is interacting with an AI system
nodes.statutoryCore: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a reasonably well-informed person.
humanJudgementTerms: obvious to a reasonably well-informed person
nodes.derivationRule: aiInvolvement in [model-assisted, model-generated] AND outputModality in [natural-language-to-human, ui-render]
nodes.havenTestForm: skeleton invariant, same mechanism as purpose://skeleton.owner-entity-access: the rendered surface must carry a visible AI disclosure.

nodes.title: Mark synthetic output in a machine-readable format
nodes.statutoryCore: Providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall ensure the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.
nodes.graceScope: systems already placed on the market before 2026-08-02
nodes.derivationRule: aiInvolvement == model-generated AND outputModality in [natural-language-to-human, synthetic-media]
nodes.havenTestForm: deterministic test on the output contract: generated content carries a provenance marker.

nodes.title: Inform persons exposed to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation
nodes.statutoryCore: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system.
nodes.derivationRule: domain == biometrics AND (infersEmotion == true OR deducesSensitiveAttribute == true)

nodes.title: Disclose deepfakes and AI-generated public-interest text
nodes.statutoryCore: Deployers generating or manipulating image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated. Deployers generating or manipulating text published to inform the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated, unless subject to human review and editorial responsibility.
nodes.derivationRule: outputModality == synthetic-media OR (aiInvolvement == model-generated AND publishedToPublic == true)

nodes.title: General-purpose AI model provider obligations
nodes.statutoryCore: Technical documentation, information for downstream providers, a copyright policy, and a sufficiently detailed public summary of training content. Article 53(2) provides a partial exemption for models released under a free and open-source licence, which does not extend to models with systemic risk.
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: HAVEN routes to models rather than publishing them. The live question is whether the Norwegian LoRA adapter work makes HAVEN a downstream provider or a model provider.

nodes.title: Obligations for GPAI models with systemic risk
nodes.statutoryCore: Model evaluation, adversarial testing, systemic risk assessment and mitigation, serious incident reporting, and cybersecurity protection.
nodes.havenRelevanceNote: Not applicable at any plausible HAVEN scale. Recorded so the not-applicable finding is documented rather than assumed.

nodes.title: Free and open-source licence exemption
nodes.statutoryCore: The Regulation does not apply to AI systems released under free and open-source licences, unless they are placed on the market or put into service as high-risk AI systems, or fall under Article 5 or Article 50.
nodes.derivationRule: licenceIsFOSS == true AND NOT (isHighRisk OR triggersArticle5 OR triggersArticle50)

nodes.title: Purely personal non-professional deployer activity
nodes.statutoryCore: The Regulation does not apply to obligations of deployers who are natural persons using AI systems in the course of a purely personal non-professional activity.
nodes.scopeNote: Exempts the deployer's obligations only. Provider obligations are untouched.

nodes.title: Pre-market research, testing and development
nodes.statutoryCore: The Regulation does not apply to research, testing or development activity regarding AI systems or AI models prior to their being placed on the market or put into service. Testing in real world conditions is not covered by this exclusion.
nodes.scopeNote: The carve-out from the carve-out matters: a HAVEN pilot at a live conference with real participants is testing in real world conditions, not pre-market development.

nodes.title: Annex III derogation where the system does not pose significant risk
nodes.statutoryCore: An AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk where it does not pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision-making, subject to enumerated conditions and a documented assessment. The derogation never applies where the system performs profiling of natural persons.
nodes.derivationRule: annexIIIHit == true AND decisionEffect == informational AND performsProfiling == false
nodes.criticalNote: This is the reason obligations must NOT be propagated by tree inheritance. A child purpose under an Annex III area can fall out of high-risk on its own facts.
